pool.text: The capture coincided with the decline of Angkor though the abandonment reasons remain unclear.
King Ang Chan named the town after repulsing an invading Thai army.
European visitors including Antonio da Madalena had visited the temple ruins much earlier.
The French School of the Far East began a long association with Angkor.
Provinces were ceded to French Indochina after being under Siamese administration for centuries.
The Grand Hotel d'Angkor opened and the temples became a leading tourist draw.
The city population was driven into the countryside by the communist Khmer Rouge.
Artisans Angkor was founded to revive traditional Khmer craftsmanship and provide rural employment.
Relative stability and a rejuvenated tourist industry revived the city after Pol Pot's death.
The Cambodian Cultural Village opened and assembled miniatures of famous historical buildings.
Over half a million foreign visitors arrived in Siem Reap Province that year.
The Angkor National Museum opened to offer visitors a better understanding of archaeological treasures.
It was estimated that over 50% of jobs in the town related to tourism.
Angkor Panorama Museum opened and housed a panorama mural depicting Khmer Empire scenes.
Authorities issued an order banning the buying, selling and butchering of dogs for food.
Lotus Silk Farm opened as a sustainable social enterprise for lotus silk weaving.
